article_content: Carino Japanese Bistro is giving a discount to parents of young, well-behaved children. Allan Welsh, his daughter, Evie, was eating at the Calgary restaurant on Mother's Day when they found a $5 discount for visiting customers on their bill. 'The $5 was for well-behaved kids,' the Rossi family shared. Tanya Rossi, 33, said on Facebook that it was a nice surprise. Allan Welsh shared the bistro's picture of their meal, including the discount, on Reddit. Scott Parbooke, the restaurant's owner, told KMGH-TV he didn't mass-produce the coupons & would still present them to new customers as an ice-breaker.

article_content: A prestigious Massachusetts academy, previously attended by Senator Ted Kennedy, has revealed that two black teachers were targeted by race hate letters from someone within the private school. Milton Academy has started a thorough investigation into these letters, which were received in late October following a diversity meeting. One letter was sent to Milton's K-8 multicultural director, while another was addressed to the school's lower-school director. The origins of the letters, their contents, and the identity of the sender remain speculative. Milton Police Chief Richard G. Wells Jr. and head of the academy Todd Bland are both engaged in quietly examining the situation. Todd Bland has chosen to inform parents directly, with a preference for confidentiality to avoid further spreading rumors. He has urged the parents to support the school's commitment to anti-hate and inclusion values. The school reflects on the racial tension in the nation, particularly regarding the grand jury decisions related to cases like Michael Brown and Eric Garner. Despite this, black students comprise a significant portion of the student body in K-8 and the upper school.

Milton Academy hat eine gründliche Untersuchung zu diesen Postings eingeleitet, die kürzlich im Oktober eingegangen sind und nach einem Treffen zur Diversitätsgrundlage stattfand. Eine Posting wurde an die Dirigentin der K-8-Multikultur an der Akademie gesendet, während die andere für die direkt an die Schüler gerichtete Direktorenbüro in den unteren Klassenplatte geschickt wurde. Der Ursprung der Postings sowie deren Inhalt und der Werfer sind spekulativ, und sowohl der Kopfinspektor der Polizei, Richard G. Wells, Jr., als auch der Leiter der Akademie, Todd Bland, sind interessiert, das Geschehen privat zu untersuchen. Todd Bland hat Eltern direkt über die Postings informiert und um Diskretion gebeten, um weitere Gerüchte zu vermeiden. Er bittet die Eltern, sich dem Komitee der Akademie in ihrer Wertschätzung gegen Hass und Inklusion zu beteiligen. Die Akademie reflektiert über die rassische Spannung in der Nation, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit den Gerichtsurteilen im Fall von Michael Brown und Eric Garner und pflegt eine deutliche Präsenz von schwarzen Schülern in K-8 und der oberen Schule.
